title: Making Suggestions and Invitations
goal: Propose an activity, invite someone, and respond with acceptance, a refusal, uncertainty or another idea.

rows.text: Why don't we meet at the park?

runs.text: proposes something to do together. In

study.title: Decline or keep the answer open

runs.text: You can decline without inventing enthusiasm or an excuse. Choose what you want the other person to understand.
You prefer not to do it.
I don't feel like going out tonight.
You do not want that activity now.
You are not joining this occasion.
Maybe. Let me check my schedule.
You have not decided or confirmed.

runs.text: Great. Let's choose a movie later.

runs.text: This is a direct exchange. Its meaning comes from the words, relationship and delivery; directness is not automatically an insult.

practice.title: Find a plan—or accept there isn't one

runs.text: Use this fictional activity card. On your own, read the invitation and speak the reply, then rehearse the inviter's response.
Suggest the walk using two different patterns. Your partner answers
Invite a friend to game night. Their role wants to join. Rehearse a complete three-turn exchange.
Your role dislikes games and wants a quiet evening. Decline game night and suggest the movie instead. Support:
Change the response: the friend says
. Answer without treating it as a firm acceptance. Support:
Change your intention: you do not want any alternative plan this weekend. Give a clear refusal and let the inviter acknowledge it.
Hide the activity card. Make one invitation with invented details. Give a different answer from the one in the model and continue coherently.
Let's take a walk Saturday afternoon. / How about taking a walk? — Sounds good. — Great.
Do you want to join us for game night? — Sure. Count me in. — Great. I'll send you the details.
I'll pass on game night. How about a movie at home instead? — That works for me.
No, thanks. I don't want to make plans this weekend. — Okay, no problem.
Was the activity clear? Could the inviter tell whether the answer was yes, no or unconfirmed? Did a refusal remain a refusal even when no explanation was given?
